text:
Rafael Mendes: proposing we standardize a quick on-call checklist for when we get pulled into a Private restore (customer drill or real incident). Right now every handoff is a different shape and we burn 20–30m just collecting basics.

Rafael Mendes: Draft checklist (v0). Would love edits/additions:
1) Who is IC / who is operator on customer side?
2) Restore type: in-place vs new cluster/VPC
3) Deployment mode: VPC k8s vs on-prem (air-gapped yes/no)
4) Cluster identifiers: customer name, cluster name, region, k8s version
5) Redwood Private version + installer/helm chart versions
6) Target RTO/RPO + maintenance window end time
7) Backup location + backend (S3/minio/NFS/etc) + encryption mode (SSE-KMS / client-side)
8) Last successful backup timestamp + size + verify status
9) DB mode: pg_dump only vs PITR/WAL archiving configured
10) Access: what role are we using (break-glass?) + how to obtain (approvals)
11) Current failure mode / logs links
12) What steps already attempted (commands pasted)
13) Validation plan after restore (smoke test endpoints)
14) Evidence capture requirements (screenshots/log bundles) if regulated

Rafael Mendes: Links to the current draft runbooks folks are using:
- In-place restore: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/runbook-private-restore-in-place
- Restore to new cluster: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/runbook-private-restore-to-new-cluster
- Backup create/verify: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/runbook-private-backup-create-and-verify

Sean Gallagher: +1. We should also explicitly ask for "Is the cluster paused / intentionally not taking backups" because it affects alert noise + expectations.

Sean Gallagher: Also add "Are we in maintenance mode already?" and "did write-path blocking kick in". We’ve seen confusion when the customer thinks the API is broken but it’s just `maintenance_mode=true`.

Talia Benson: Love this. Suggest we format as a copy/paste block for #incidents + a smaller version for paging someone in.

Talia Benson: Handoff fields I’d add:
- Timezone + preferred comms channel (Zoom bridge? Slack Connect?)
- Change ticket / approval reference (if enterprise)
- Any hard constraints: no outbound internet, no new IAM roles, no DNS change, etc.

Markus Klein: From Solutions POV, please include:
- Customer contact + escalation path (who can approve break-glass)
- Whether Redwood is expected to drive keyboard or just advise
- "What is the business impact" / what service is down (control plane only vs inference traffic)

Fatima Noor: For on-prem/air-gapped, we need a specific prompt:
- Is there a staging repo mounted? what path? (NFS mount / local PVC)
- How are images/artifacts moved offline? (USB / bastion / internal registry)
- Any file size limits in the staging system (we’ve hit this on bundle uploads)

Connor O'Brien: +1. Also request versions *and* hashes when possible. We’ve had restores fail because they’re mixing installer 0.9.x with chart values from 0.10.x.

Connor O'Brien: Maybe add a line for the exact command invoked:
```
rw-private-dr restore plan --config ...
rw-private-dr restore execute --plan ...
```
Plus `--debug` logs and where they were uploaded.

Elliot Price: If this is going into docs, can we keep the checklist consistent with the doc nav/terminology? We’ve been trying to standardize on “Private DR toolkit” and “backup verify” language.

Elliot Price: Also can we include links to the sections inside the runbooks (anchors) vs top-level? Folks don’t scroll.

Kira Thompson: I can turn this into a “Restore assistance intake” template page + a Slack snippet. If you want, we can also add it as a short section at the top of both restore runbooks (“Before you start: gather these inputs”).

Sean Gallagher: Another thing: ask for object storage endpoint connectivity from the cluster.
- For S3: are VPC endpoints / gateway endpoints in place? DNS resolution ok?
- Any recent IAM/KMS changes?

Sean Gallagher: (this is basically the root cause of 50% of “restore stuck” cases)

Rafael Mendes: good call. Adding explicit "connectivity precheck" row.

incident-bot: Reminder: use /backup-status to pull latest backup age + dashboard links if the cluster is emitting metrics. (Configured for some Private installs.)

Rafael Mendes: oh nice, didn’t know that existed. Do we also have a restore checklist shortcut?

Kira Thompson: There’s a PR in flight for `/restore-checklist` that just links to the runbooks + the intake template. Not merged yet but soon.

Markus Klein: For enterprise drills, include “DNS/TLS cutover plan” if restore-to-new-cluster. Who owns certs, how fast can they change DNS, is there a pre-provisioned cert, etc.

Fatima Noor: +1 and if on-prem: “does the new cluster share the same internal FQDN naming” or is it an IP-based access. DNS changes can be non-trivial.

Connor O'Brien: We should also add one explicit safety gate to the checklist: confirm we have a verified backup BEFORE doing anything destructive (scale down, wipe PVCs, etc). Like a “stop sign” in the template.

Sean Gallagher: yes please. Also include “do we need to attach evidence” (Olga’s team has asked us to keep a consistent evidence bundle: logs + timestamps + who approved).

Rafael Mendes: ok updated v0.2 (copy/paste format):

Rafael Mendes: 
```
PRIVATE RESTORE ASSISTANCE INTAKE (paste + fill)

Owner/Comms
- IC:
- Operator (customer):
- Redwood on-call:
- Comms: (Slack Connect / Zoom link):
- Timezone:
- Change ticket / approval ref:

Context
- Customer / env / cluster name:
- Deployment: (VPC k8s | on-prem)  Air-gapped: (Y/N)
- Restore type: (in-place | new cluster)
- Target RTO/RPO + maintenance window ends at:
- Business impact: (control plane down? inference down? admin only?)

Versions
- Redwood Private version:
- Installer version:
- Helm chart version + values bundle ref:
- k8s version + storage class details:

Backup Details (STOP if unknown)
- Backup backend: (S3/minio/NFS/other)
- Location/bucket/path:
- Encryption: (SSE-KMS | SSE-S3 | client-side)  KMS key ref:
- Last successful backup ts + size:
- `backup verify` run? (Y/N) output/link:
- DB mode: (pg_dump | PITR/WAL)  WAL archive destination:

Access
- What credentials/role are being used:
- Break-glass needed? (Y/N) Approval obtained from:
- Network constraints: (no outbound / private endpoints only / proxy):

Prechecks
- Storage endpoint connectivity from cluster verified? (Y/N) notes:
- Maintenance mode set? (Y/N)  Write paths blocked as expected? (Y/N)

What happened
- Symptom + exact error:
- Commands already run (paste):
- Logs location (link/path):

Plan
- Which runbook: (in-place | new cluster) link:
- Validation gates: (health checks + smoke test endpoints) owner:
- Evidence to capture (logs/screenshots/timestamps):
```

Rafael Mendes: Reactions welcome, and if folks agree I’ll pin + ask Docs to publish as a snippet.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: please add one more line under Prechecks: “DB lock contention / peak traffic?” (we’ve had customers try to run restore while traffic is still hammering the DB).

Connor O'Brien: :+1: Also add “Are backups suspended by policy” (some clusters disable CronJobs during upgrades).

Elliot Price: Works for me. If you send me the final text, I’ll coordinate with Kira to place it at top of the restore runbooks and in the Day-2 ops overview page.

Kira Thompson: I’ll draft the Confluence template page today and link it from both restore runbooks + the on-call snippet. Rafael, DM me any preferred naming (I’ll keep it consistent with “Private DR toolkit”).

Markus Klein: looks solid. This will help a lot for the pilot customers; we can pre-fill half of this during kickoff.

Fatima Noor: Can you add one on-prem specific line under Backup Details: “bundle format + transport method” (mounted repo vs copied tar/zstd). Otherwise looks good.

Rafael Mendes: yep, adding on-prem line + Sean’s DB contention note. I’ll repost v0.3 once updated and pin it. Thanks all.
